The Elephant: Why We Buy What We Buy

01 · The Problem

Why did I buy this? The assignment asked me to examine a personal possession, unpack the thought process behind buying it, iterate on that thinking, and explain what my reasoning reveals about design and human behavior. I selected a hand-carved pink stone elephant I purchased from a craftsman in Udaipur, India.

02 · My Role

This was an individual project. I sketched and annotated the object myself, documenting its physical and emotional properties and positioning it against alternatives I consciously chose not to buy.

03 · How I Came to My Solution

I used ergonomic observation to sketch out the details. The object is hand-carved, which shows intricacy and detail. It is made of light pink stone that adds a feminine touch. It has a stable form that sits still. It features an elephant inside an elephant, demonstrating craft, complexity, and precision. Its compact size means it does not occupy too much space in a small apartment.

I then compared it to competitors I would not choose: mass-produced decor (I prefer uniqueness) and factory-made souvenirs (I prefer handcraft).

"Watching the craftsman carve this in Udaipur made it meaningful. It reflects my value for culture, home, handcraft, and giving back to society. When I feel low, this reminds me of home. Matching pieces with friends keeps us connected."
04 · How It Solved the Problem

By analyzing what the object does physically and what it means emotionally, I built a framework for understanding why people keep certain things close. The elephant is not just decor. It is a connection to culture, a reminder of home, and a shared symbol with friends who own matching pieces.

05 · Challenges

The easy route was to describe the object visually. The harder work was pushing past that into emotional honesty: articulating why the pink stone specifically matters, why compact size is important when you live in a New York apartment, and why the elephant-inside-elephant detail makes it irreplaceable to me.

06 · How It Affected Me

This exercise reframed how I think about design. Products that endure in people's lives carry layers of meaning: cultural, social, sensory, and emotional. Understanding why I kept this object makes me a more empathetic designer for others.

07 · What I Learned

The emotional depth behind why we buy something far outweighs functional reasoning. Ergonomics, aesthetics, cultural resonance, and personal narrative all intersect in the objects we choose to keep. Great design understands and honors all four layers.
